about: Outbound licence policy for scripts/check-licences.mjs. BE RELAX is a closed-source commercial product for a single business, so the question this policy answers is not 'is this open source' but 'what does distributing it oblige us to publish'. Strong copyleft in the shipped closure is refused outright and cannot be accepted; weak copyleft in the shipped closure needs an entry in `accepted` recording the obligation it carries; weak copyleft that only ever runs on a build machine is allowed without an entry, because MPL and LGPL obligations attach to conveying the work, not to compiling with it.

platformBinaries.reason: Prebuilt libvips. Read from the installed linux-x64 build; the other platforms carry the same licence and are declared here so a macOS or musl target is classified on a Linux runner rather than skipped. Listed before @img/sharp-* because the first matching pattern wins.
sharp's own native bindings, confirmed against the installed @img/sharp-linux-x64.
Confirmed against the installed lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu. Build tooling only — it arrives through tailwindcss, which is a devDependency of apps/web.
Declared upstream. Never installed on any platform here: it is an optional peer of sharp's WASM build, which this deployment does not use.
Declared upstream. macOS-only, so never installed on a Linux runner.

accepted.reason: The only copyleft dependency this product distributes. sharp ships prebuilt libvips shared libraries; libvips is LGPL-3.0-or-later and nothing else in the image derives from it. Replacing sharp is not a serious option — it is the image pipeline W-SYS-05 is built on — and the LGPL does not ask us to open anything, so the finding is recorded rather than removed.
accepted.obligation: The deployed image must carry libvips' LGPL text and notice, and the offer to supply or replace the library must be honoured. The library is linked unmodified and is not statically linked into our code; if that ever changes this entry stops being sufficient. The notice ships with the image, so the duty lands on the unit that writes apps/worker/Dockerfile (W-SYS-06).
accepted.dischargedBy: W-SYS-06. apps/worker/Dockerfile asserts /usr/share/common-licenses/LGPL-3 and GPL-3 are present (LGPL-3.0 incorporates GPL-3.0 by reference), records the installed libvips version at /usr/share/berelax/libvips-version.txt, and copies apps/worker/licences/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md — which carries the notice and the written offer — into the image. scripts/check-container.mjs enforces all of it by rule name. Worth recording, because it is why the obligation could not be discharged by copying node_modules: the @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64 package ships NO copy of the LGPL text.

nonNpmShippedComponents.about: What this product distributes that this gate structurally cannot see. It reads pnpm-lock.yaml, so an operating-system package in the worker image is invisible to it, and the obligation a prebuilt binary package carries can be about what the IMAGE ships rather than about what the graph contains. Both are governed by build/container-policy.json's imageComponents, which is where the notice, the licence text path and the written offer are enforced by pnpm container. This block is the cross-reference, and scripts/check-licences.mjs fails in both directions if the two files stop agreeing about which components exist. No licence string is duplicated here — only the name — because two copies of a classification is one copy that can be wrong.
nonNpmShippedComponents.ffmpeg: W-SYS-06's hero video encoder, installed by apt into apps/worker/Dockerfile. GPL-2.0-or-later, not LGPL: ffmpeg's own code is LGPL-2.1-or-later, but Debian configures it --enable-gpl so that libx264 and libx265 can be included, and ffmpeg's configure refuses either without it. That is not avoidable by choosing a different build. docs/08 §6 and W-SYS-06's acceptance specify -profile:v high and -crf, which are x264/x265 options, and the LGPL-compatible encoders do not reach them: OpenH264 is Constrained Baseline with no CRF, and kvazaar covers HEVC only. So a strong-copyleft component is accepted in a way the `accepted` array above could not express — and the reason the npm rule's remedy (`remove the dependency`) does not apply is that ffmpeg is a separate process invoked over an argument vector, not a linked library, so the obligation is to convey ITS source and licence and does not reach BE RELAX's code. A native binding or a static link would change that completely.
nonNpmShippedComponents.libvips: Already accepted above as @img/sharp-libvips-* because it IS in the graph. It is also named here because the obligation H-HARD-02 recorded is that the deployed image carries the LGPL text and honours the offer, and the package ships no copy of that text at all — README.md, package.json, versions.json and lib/, nothing else. An image built from node_modules would carry the library without its licence, and no npm gate could say so.
nonNpmShippedComponents.patents: Y12-video-patents. AVC and HEVC are covered by patent pools that copyright licences say nothing about. Whether encoding and self-hosting a short decorative loop owes anything is a legal question rather than a build decision; the provisional position is the strict one, and no real footage has been encoded.
